_comment: §2c of api-growth-method.md, run 2026-07-30 at the end of slice A. This is
the BASELINE: the run later ones improve on. Script:
docs/planning/engine/slice-evidence/blind-agent-runs/SCRIPT.md
⚠ CONTAMINATION, stated rather than hidden. Two exposures, both biasing
TOWARD competence — so the failures below are trustworthy and the successes
are weaker than they look:
1. a subagent in this repository inherits AGENTS.md through its system
prompt, which a genuine third party would not have;
2. the fixed script and the evidence tree were filed under docs/sdk/ when
this run launched — the one directory the agent was told to start from.
Moved to docs/planning/engine/slice-evidence/ mid-run. The agent's
report shows no sign of having read either, but 'no sign' is not proof,
and a measurement whose contamination is written down is worth more
than one that looks clean.
⚠ THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS MISLEADING AND THE AGENT SAID SO ITSELF. It opened
no `.rs` file under crates/. It also ran `cargo doc` over SEVEN engine crates
and read the rendered API, which it correctly called 'the same information a
leak would have given me, just laundered through rustdoc'. Scoring this run
on `.rs` files opened would report a pass. `first_engine_file_opened` is
therefore recorded as the Cargo.lock it actually opened first, and
`engine_api_surfaces_read` carries the seven — because the gate ADR 0031
states is 'never opening a file under crates/', and rustdoc over a crate is
reading that crate.
run.harness: fresh general-purpose subagent, no inherited conversation context

completed.notes: Headless COMPILES AND RUNS but activates nothing — see reachable_empty_host below; the agent's own verdict was 'headless boots, but a minimal game it is not'. Windowed was blocked by the environment (no X/Wayland/Xvfb), not by the API; the agent proved the composition instead via `without_gpu()`, which ran the full render graph to completion.

run.first_engine_file_reason: To find out whether the reference consumer also pins bevy_ggrs to a git fork, after a fresh lockfile resolved bevy_ggrs 0.21.0 from crates.io and the engine failed to compile. NOT an API question — a BUILDABILITY question, and it came before any API question could be asked.

engine_api_surfaces_read.looking_for: the real signatures of mount/build/run/without_gpu/with_game_assets — docs/sdk/ shows call sites but no method list
how to satisfy `PlatformerAssetsPlugin found no CharacterCatalog`
whether an empty default catalog provider ships (it does not)
how to construct the RoomMetadata that ModuleDraft::room wants
whether the sprite side needs its own registration before a visible host builds
what makes a route REAL, after finding the headless host had zero entities
how to satisfy `frontend audio provider registered no audio fragment`
whether the audio fragment also needed an SfxProvider (it did not)

findings.summary: The engine does not compile for an outside consumer at all without copying `[patch.crates-io] bevy_ggrs = { git = ..., rev = ... }` out of the engine's workspace-root Cargo.toml. A fresh lockfile resolves bevy_ggrs 0.21.0 from crates.io and ambition_runtime fails with `cannot find type GgrsFrameTiming in crate bevy_ggrs`.
findings.why_it_matters: It precedes every API question. No amount of work on `ambition::app` reaches a third party who cannot get past `cargo check`. The fixture's own Cargo.toml records this as a known leak; docs/sdk/ never mentions it, so the knowledge existed and was not where a consumer would look.
findings.agents_words: the single highest-value missing paragraph in the whole SDK

findings.summary: `ambition::app`'s module docs say 'Rule 7 is not enforced by ordering but by TYPE ... the empty host is unreachable rather than merely documented.' What is enforced is that a STRING was supplied. `gameplay_route("blind_run/gameplay")` naming a route no experience registered builds clean, runs 60 ticks, and spawns ZERO entities — exactly the failure rule 7 describes.
findings.why_it_matters: A doc that overclaims its own headline guarantee is worse than one that claims nothing: the agent only found the empty host because it independently counted entities. This is the campaign's own rule 2 violated in the campaign's own code — a doc marker standing where a check should be.
findings.fix_named_by_the_agent: validate declared routes against the ShellRouteCatalog at try_build

findings.summary: api-prototype.md §2b states the two faces 'differ in policy, not in structure: same modules, same order, same routes.' False in the shipped builder: the visible face installs PlatformerAssetsPlugin, which panics without a CharacterCatalog. A module that boots headless does not boot windowed.
findings.why_it_matters: The doc actively told the agent the opposite of what is true, which is the most expensive kind of wrong. Note this is the SAME seam §2d flagged: `with_game_assets` made the faces diverge, and the divergence has a second consequence nobody had written down.

findings.summary: `ModuleDraft::capability` requires `Clone`, and the engine's own `CharacterCatalogPlugin` does not implement it — so an engine plugin cannot go through the engine's own capability slot. Every consumer writes the same wrapper.
findings.why_it_matters: Introduced by A3, in the deferred-install closure. Not a doc gap.

findings.summary: There is no supported read-model for 'did my game actually start?'. The agent fell back to `app.world().entities().len()`, which is raw Bevy and says nothing about routes.
findings.why_it_matters: Four of the eight rules `ambition::app` owns fail SILENTLY. An API with silent failure modes and no assertion surface makes every consumer invent the same smoke test — badly.

findings.summary: api-prototype.md §3 shows `.experience(OUTLANDER_EXPERIENCE).launcher_route(OUTLANDER_LAUNCHER_ROUTE).room(outlander_room().metadata).capability(OutlanderExperiencePlugin)` — every identifier is undefined. The agent could not tell whether they were `&str`, newtypes or consts, and guessed.
findings.why_it_matters: For a document whose acceptance test is 'an agent can do this from docs alone', a non-runnable example is the core defect, not a nitpick.

findings.summary: `CharacterCatalogPlugin` takes a raw RON string with no documented schema and no `Default`. The agent recovered `(brain_presets: {}, action_set_presets: {}, characters: {})` by feeding it `"()"` and scripting a loop over the resulting 'Unexpected missing field named X' errors.

docs/sdk/ never shows a Cargo.toml: not where the `ambition` crate lives, not what bevy version to pin, not the patch table. The README also tells a consumer to add `bevy` themselves, which is wrong — `ambition` already does `pub use bevy;`.

what_worked: The `build()` panic listing ALL THREE missing declarations at once — the agent called it 'genuinely the best diagnostic in the run'. ADR 0032's 'errors arrive once, structured, at a known point' paid off.

Rules 1 and 2 are really engine-owned: `without_gpu()` loaded 4/4 parallax layers with the process cwd at /tmp, which is only possible if the asset source and the engine asset root were installed correctly without the consumer saying anything.

`without_gpu()` ALSO survives having no display server. Undocumented, and it is the property a headless-CI reader is looking for. api-prototype.md §7 asked whether it belongs on the public builder; the consumer's answer was 'yes, unambiguously'.
run.verdict: Slice A's composition claims are TRUE where the engine takes ownership (rules 1-6, 8) and OVERCLAIMED where it only documents (rule 7). The binding constraint on this engine is not an API leak at all: a third party cannot compile it.

criteria.evidence: Untouched, and NOT slice A's to touch. The barrier is process-global: Mary-O, Sanic, the versus fighters and the robot lineage all still stage through it, so an Outlander-only slice cannot make it deletable. This is the criterion whose misplacement forced the campaign's A-D split.

⚠ RECLASSIFIED 2026-07-30. Previously marked composition/deletable on the strength of the green hand-ordering contract. That contract is about HOST composition order; this criterion is about CONTENT completeness, which is still decided by `Plugin::build` running `install_outlander_content` and by the finish/PreStartup apparatus slice A never went near. `define` accumulating into a draft is the shape that will close it, but the draft holds routes and a room in slice A, not content.
content-model criterion; the idempotence flag is untouched (slice B+)

⚠ MOVED AWAY from deletable, and this is the sharpest thing slice A measured. `PlatformerApp` gained `with_game_assets`, OFF by default on headless and always on for windowed — so the two faces now consume different prepared art unless the consumer says otherwise. That was a deliberate correction (the first draft installed assets on both faces citing THIS criterion, and the fixture's rollback parity test caught it: under GGRS the extra asset frames are frames the sim does not advance, and the two hosts landed twelve `update()` calls apart). Preparing art is also not free — boot decode was measured at 627MP/2.5GB. So the knob is right and the criterion is further away, which is a real finding rather than a regression: the criterion wants ONE FINGERPRINT, and slice A has no content fingerprint to share. Slice B owns closing it, and must close it without collapsing the policy back into the face.
content-model criterion; no module-qualified namespaces exist yet (slice B)
content-model criterion; the fallback catalog is untouched (slice B)

capability_footprint.note: The consumer declares two dependencies (`ambition`, `bevy`) and links the whole engine closure. A module allowlist cannot see this: slice A's ratchet went from 18 to 14 while this number did not move at all, which is precisely the blind spot §2e exists to record.

selects_slice_b.one_leak: a consumer cannot stand up a SMALL game — the visible host demands content a minimal module has no way to supply, and there is no way to check whether the host came up at all.
